also: the flight has been put back

terms.comment: An ordinary description, a flight put off: volātus, a flight (Egger, in M-O s.v. flight), and differō, differre, distulī, dīlātum, to put off, to delay (Cic., Caes., in Lewis & Short). Traupman and Morgan–Owens have no phrase for a delayed flight.

phrases.english: We’ll have to wait a little.

phrases.latin: Volātus noster in hōram nōnam dīlātus est.
phrases.english: Our flight has been put back to nine o’clock.

phrases.latin: Āëroplanum nostrum hōrā sērius abscēdet; interim lūdāmus.
phrases.english: Our plane will leave an hour late; let’s play in the meantime.

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. flight (airplane).
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 216.
